assessment.question:
### Exercise 12.11: Calculate the area of irregular shapes

4. In the shape below, one of the lengths of the sides has been replaced by $z$. The other five sides have the lengths shown. All of the angles are right angles, as labelled.

Determine the value of $z$. Then find the area of this shape. All lengths are in mm.
assessment.expected_answer:
Start by finding $z$. All the angles are right angles, so you can use the sides parallel to $z$, which are 4 mm and 5 mm long.

$$
\begin{array}{ll}
z & {= 4 + 5} \\
& {= 9}
\end{array}
$$

Now we break the shape into two rectangles to find the area.

$$
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{Area}_{A} & {= l \times b} \\
 & {= 9 \times 5} \\
 & {= \text{45 mm}^{2}} \\
\text{Area}_{B} & {= l \times b} \\
 & {= 4 \times 4} \\
 & {= \text{16 mm}^{2}} \\
\text{Area}_\text{Total} & {= \text{Area}_{A} + \text{Area}_{B}} \\
 & {= \text{61 mm}^{2}} \\
\end{array}
$$

assessment.question:
### Exercise 12.12: Find perimeter and area in real life situations

5. Talatu paints plates to sell to tourists. She paints the plates purple with a white circle in the centre.

The diagram below shows the plate. $O$ is the centre of the plate. The radius of the small white circle is 3 cm and the radius of the big blue circle is 7 cm.

Determine the area of the purple region. Use 3.14 for $\pi$.
assessment.expected_answer:
To calculate the area of the purple region, you need to calculate the area of each of the two circles, and then subtract one area from the other.

**Area of big circle:**

$$
\begin{array}{ll}
A_\text{1} & {= \pi \times R^{2}} \\
& {= 3.14 \times 7^{2}} \\
& {= 3.14 \times 49} \\
& {= 153.86\ {\text{cm}^{2}}} \\
\end{array}
$$

**Area of small circle:**

$$
\begin{array}{ll}
A_\text{2} & {= \pi \times r^{2}} \\
& {= 3.14 \times 3^{2}} \\
& {= 3.14 \times 9} \\
& {= 28.26\ {\text{cm}^{2}}} \\
\end{array}
$$

**Area of purple region:**

$$
\begin{array}{ll}
A & {= A_\text{1} - A_\text{2}} \\
& {= 153.86 - 28.26} \\
& {= \text{125.6}\ {\text{cm}^{2}}}
\end{array}
$$

The area of the purple region is 125.6 cm$^{2}$.
